# RustyNES v2.9.6 — "Roster"

The mapper release of the line to v3.0.0. **17 new mapper families (174 → 191)**, all written from their NESdev pages. GTROM is promoted to Curated, self-flashing homebrew boards keep their saves, and mapper 4's NES 2.0 submappers are corrected.

## New mapper families

- **MMC3 multicarts and variants:**
  - 12 (SL-5020B);
  - 37 (*Super Mario Bros. + Tetris + Nintendo World Cup*);
  - 45 (GA23C);
  - 47 (*Super Spike V'Ball + Nintendo World Cup*);
  - 121 (Kasheng);
  - 249 (Waixing T9552).
- **Waixing boards that mix CHR-ROM and CHR-RAM:** 74, 191, 192, 194, and 195, where a PPU write picks which banks are RAM.
- **Cony / Yoko (83)**, all three variants, with the 16-bit CPU-cycle IRQ.
- **J.Y. Company (91)**, with both of its IRQ counters.
- **NES-EVENT (105)**, the *Nintendo World Championships 1990* cartridge, with its lock and its 30-bit timer at the tournament setting.
- **Bandai LZ93D50 with battery RAM (153)**, *Famicom Jump II*.
- **Nanjing FC-001 (163)**, with its automatic CHR-RAM switch.
- **Action 52 / Cheetahmen II (228).**

Of the 191 families, **160 are accuracy-gated** (51 Core, 109 Curated). The other 31 are BestEffort, where the documentation is thin, and are kept out of every accuracy claim. None of the new families has a redistributable commercial ROM, so each is pinned by unit tests from its register description and by a synthetic program run on the whole emulator.

## Fixes

- **Mapper 4's NES 2.0 submappers were mis-assigned.** Submapper 1 is the **MMC6**, and it now has its own 1 KiB RAM with per-half enables; before, it ran as a different MMC3. Submapper 4 is the NEC MMC3. Submappers 2 (hard-wired mirroring), 3 (Acclaim MC-ACC) and 5 (the T9552 scrambler) are now modelled. **StarTropics** with a NES 2.0 header is the game this reaches. Its RAM at `$7000` read as zero and dropped every write before. It now works.
- **GTROM (111)** matches its documentation: the register decodes only where the hardware decodes it, a read of it latches the floating bus, `$3000-$3EFF` is bonus RAM rather than a mirror, and the flash chip can be rewritten.
- **Self-flashing games keep their saves.** GTROM and UNROM 512 (30) games save by rewriting their own flash chip, and RustyNES now emulates that chip. The save persists like a battery save on desktop, Android, iOS and RetroArch.
- **UNROM 512's four-screen board** now has true four-screen nametables.
- **The *Ninja Ryukenden* mapper-111 image** is a different board, an MMC1 variant with no public register description. It is now refused with a clear message; before, it ran as GTROM and froze at once.

## Save states

Save states for the boards changed here carry new layouts. States for Bandai FCG (16, 159) and MMC3 boards from earlier releases still load. **GTROM and UNROM 512 states from v2.9.5 or earlier do not load**, and fail with a version error rather than being misread.

## Verification

- The full `--features test-roms` suite passes: 3,021 tests, 0 failed, 20 ignored. AccuracyCoin is 144/144 and nestest is 0-diff.
- Every new behaviour is pinned by a test that fails when it is reverted: 31 of 31 mutants are caught.
- The local commercial suites pass without re-blessing: 6/0, 138/0 and 60/0. They had not been re-checked since about v2.0.0; each changed snapshot was attributed against a clean `main` before it was accepted, and only StarTropics changed because of this release.
- fmt, clippy for every feature set and all three wasm builds, rustdoc, the `no_std` build, cargo-deny, the release audits and every pre-commit hook are clean.

## The MiSTer core

The RTL is unchanged, so the bitstreams attached here are **v2.9.2's files, byte for byte**: on-die md5 `c17b0f37d5c49b150c023734b583f468`, off-die md5 `75ae3a99e840e29675ded9898dae127d`. **No hardware has run any bitstream.**

## Install

- Download the pre-built binaries for Linux, macOS, and Windows below.
- The MiSTer core bitstreams are attached below: `RustyNES_MiSTer-v2.9.6.rbf` (on-die, also as `RustyNES_20260928.rbf`) and `RustyNES_MiSTer-v2.9.6-offdie.rbf`. They are v2.9.2's files, so the MiSTer menu shows build date 260928. Neither has run on hardware.
- The WebAssembly build is live at [doublegate.github.io/RustyNES](https://doublegate.github.io/RustyNES/).
- The RetroArch core is in RetroArch's Online Updater on the platforms the libretro buildbot publishes to.
